Hi Elena —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for your private deployment. Per our call last week, I wanted to kick off the implementation thread so we have a single source of truth for networking details, on‑prem packaging, and the mutual action plan. Next steps I propose: 

1) Confirm network contacts + CIDR ranges for VPC peering and any reserved overlap constraints.
2) Share list of IPs/domains for private endpoints and egress policy we’ll need to allow.
3) Decide whether you’ll run the on‑prem package (appliance image) in staging first or perform a direct air‑gapped install.
4) Schedule a 60‑minute technical kickoff this week to review the runbook and security checklist.

I’ve attached a short checklist and our on‑prem requirements PDF to this thread — please upload any internal network diagrams you have so we can pre‑validate.

Attachments: ASN-network-checklist.xlsx (network fields), redwood_onprem_requirements.pdf

Thanks — happy to coordinate.

Hi Elena —

Quick technical notes from our side ahead of the kickoff: 

• On‑prem package versions: we support the 3.2.x appliance image (recommended for staging) and 3.3.x (GA) for production. If you need the 3.1 branch for an air‑gapped validation, we can provide it but will require the offline checksum bundle.
• Ports: we need TCP 443 outbound for updates optionally, TCP 7443 for internal control plane (peered VPC access), and UDP 53 for split‑DNS queries if you use our private endpoints resolver.
• KV cache sizing: please confirm expected concurrent sessions and average request size; that will affect the memory profile we provision in the appliance.

I attached the onprem image manifest and a short note on which artifacts are required for air‑gapped installs.

If you prefer, we can run a preflight validation against the staging VPC before the kickoff — I recommend we do that 24–48 hours earlier to catch firewall rules.

— Camila Reyes
